Transportation Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch59.R
centrality_transportation.Rd

Transportation centrality (Piraveenan and Saripada 2023) is a betweenness in which traffic between two nodes spreads over all simple paths, a longer path carrying less: $$TC(v) = \frac{1}{(N-1)(N-2)} \sum_{s \ne v \ne t} \frac{\sum_{i \in P^v_{s,t}} e^{-\beta C_i}} {\sum_{j \in P_{s,t}} e^{-\beta C_j}},$$ where \(P_{s,t}\) holds all simple paths from \(s\) to \(t\), \(P^v_{s,t}\) those through \(v\), and \(C\) is the number of edges of a path.

Usage

centrality_transportation(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses transport_beta (the sensitivity to path length, default 0.1) and enumeration_limit.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order, between 0 and 1, or NA at every node when the score was not computed.

Details

Direction is used, and weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The pairs \((s, t)\) are ordered. transport_beta is 0.1 by default, the value the experiments of the source concentrate on; its worked example uses 2, and it states no single default. As transport_beta grows the measure tends to shortest-path betweenness divided by \((N-1)(N-2)\), and at 0 every simple path counts alike. A pair without a path adds nothing. A node with one tie scores 0. A negative transport_beta raises a cograph_bad_parameter error, and a network of fewer than three nodes gives NA with a cograph_undefined_measure warning.

The number of simple paths grows exponentially with the size and density of the network. The measure is therefore costly, computed only when requested by name or through include, and it stops after enumeration_limit search steps (default one million): every score is then NA with a cograph_undefined_measure warning.

References

Piraveenan, M. and Saripada, N. B. (2023). Transportation centrality: quantifying the relative importance of nodes in transportation networks based on traffic modeling. IEEE Access, 11, 142214-142234. doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2023.3339121 .

See also

centrality_betweenness, centrality_rsp_betweenness, centrality.

Examples

paw <- matrix(0, 4, 4, dimnames = list(1:4, 1:4))
paw[rbind(c(1, 2), c(1, 3), c(2, 3), c(3, 4))] <- 1
paw <- paw + t(paw)
centrality_transportation(paw, transport_beta = 2)
#>          1          2          3          4 
#> 0.07946861 0.07946861 0.70640097 0.00000000
